note:
Class 6B, week of 16 November. Notes for myself.

Aarav Sharma has missed four days this month. His mother Sunita told me on the phone (98765 43210) that his father lost his job at the mill and the family cannot pay for anything extra this term; Aarav now helps at the family tea stall before school. He is bright in maths but has not handed in homework for two weeks.

Meenal reads well aloud but freezes in written tests. She needs extra writing practice, and the remedial writing club meets after the last bell. She told me she has epilepsy and is afraid of having a seizure in the exam hall. Her roll no. 6B/23. She walks six kilometres home to Rampur Kalan and has to leave school at the last bell to reach home before dark.

Kabir and Ishaan fight most days during group work. Kabir's parents are separating and he is staying with his grandmother. Ishaan finishes early and gets bored.

Tanvi is far ahead in reading. She could help others, but she is shy. Her family does not have a smartphone or an internet connection.

Lesson
Class: Class 6
Subject: English
Topic: Writing a short description of a place
Length: 40 minutes

draft.title: English Practical Lesson Plan for Class 6

items.heading: Starter (5 minutes)
items.text: The teacher writes the topic of writing a short description of a place on the board and asks pupils to share quick descriptive words. The pupils call out words relating to sights and sounds while the teacher lists them. The materials needed are just the blackboard and chalk.

items.heading: Teach (10 minutes)
items.text: The teacher models how to write a short descriptive paragraph about a familiar environment using sensory details. The pupils listen and note down key structural tips in their notebooks. The materials needed are notebooks and pens.

items.heading: Practise (15 minutes)
items.text: The teacher guides the class to write their own short description of a place based on the model provided. The pupils write their paragraphs independently at their desks while the teacher circulates to offer help. The materials needed are notebooks and pens.

items.heading: Check (10 minutes)
items.text: The teacher invites a few pupils to read out their descriptions to the class. The pupils listen and give positive feedback or point out strong descriptive words used. The materials needed are the written work in the pupils notebooks.

items.heading: Homework (0 minutes)
items.text: The teacher sets the homework to write one more short paragraph describing a different room at home. The pupils copy the homework task into their notebooks. The materials needed are notebooks and pens.

4. Write one sentence about a sound you hear.

6. Combine your sentences into a short descriptive paragraph.

ticket.question: What kind of details should we include when describing a place?
ticket.answer: Sensory details like sights and sounds.

ticket.question: Give one example of a sight word.
ticket.answer: Bright (or any valid descriptive sight word).

ticket.question: Give one example of a sound word.
ticket.answer: Quiet (or any valid descriptive sound word).
